image_input: original full image, shared RGB888 pixel buffer
changes_from_v1: the canonical format table maps the underscored BarBeR labels (ROYAL_MAIL, IATA_2_OF_5, USPS_INTELLIGENT_MAIL) to the spellings the decoders use; v1 stripped the underscores before lookup and scored those annotations as unsupported for every reader
GS1 application identifiers printed in parentheses are unwrapped for CODE_128 / GS1_128, so '(90)85320' matches the annotation '9085320'
a ROYAL_MAIL payload one character shorter than the annotation counts as the same reading, because the Linux DBR build returns 10 of the 11 characters
CODE_128 and GS1_128 are one format family: GS1-128 is Code 128 carrying GS1 data (AIM ]C1 vs ]C0), not a separate symbology
no barcode-count hint is passed: a dataset-level maximum (the manifest holds images with 14 barcodes) made DBR search every 1-barcode image as if 14 were present, which cost 4.3x the decode time
unmatched_prediction_policy: a prediction that no annotation claims is not scored against any instance; BarBeR's annotations are curated rather than exhaustive, so it cannot be adjudicated
unreliable_placeholder_policy: ground truth payload '^' is excluded from scoring
decoder_order: deterministic randomized per sample and repetition
formats: all formats supported by each tested decoder
expected_barcode_count: not set — the decoder decides how many barcodes to look for
